claims.text: The proposed model integrates disorder-sensitive descriptors from advanced first-principles simulations with experimental thermal-conductivity data.
Atomic mass variance, local bond-stiffness distributions, and force-constant fluctuations are relevant descriptors for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
First-principles simulations can provide physically relevant information about fluctuations in high-entropy alloys.
Data-driven or computational design strategies can be used to screen high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.
The target high-entropy alloys exhibit significant atomic disorder in their as-synthesized state.
Phonon transport predominates at the elevated operating temperatures relevant to the proposed thermal-insulation application.
Local atomic-scale disorder and bond-stiffness fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Detailed disorder descriptors allow the model to capture the interplay between composition, lattice dynamics, and phonon scattering.
Capturing disorder-dependent phonon scattering will improve identification of compositions with suppressed phonon thermal transport.
The proposed model will predict low-phonon-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional empirical or computational models.
The proposed model will identify compositions with phonon thermal conductivities significantly lower than those identified by conventional methods.
Current empirical and conventional computational models do not accurately capture the effects of atomic disorder on phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
The approach is primarily applicable to high-entropy alloys with pronounced atomic disorder.
The approach may not be valid for ordered alloys or systems in which disorder has only a minor role in phonon transport.
Laser-flash analysis or a comparable technique can benchmark the predicted phonon thermal conductivity over the relevant temperature range.
Failure to obtain conductivity below the proposed threshold, or failure to improve significantly over conventional predictions, would falsify the hypothesis.
